answer: A verifiable reputation ledger serves as a robust defense against artificial identity saturation in multi-agent networks, functioning much like a secure canyon where only authenticated nodes pass. To prevent malicious spoofing akin to a deceptive raven in an old fable, the system demands cryptographic proofs of historical utility and staked computational capital. Consequently, an attacker attempting to flood the ecosystem faces exponential economic penalties, rendering the generation of counterfeit agent personas computationally and financially prohibitive.
